evaluation_limitations: The supplied frozen segment map is authoritative and was used without modification.
Retrieved source passages and retrieval logs were not supplied, so corpus fidelity and citation accuracy cannot be independently verified.
This is a per-run evaluation of one interview; it does not support dataset-level significance, prompt ranking, or other aggregate conclusions.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Honestly, the liaison language stuck with me a bit … I’d let the imagery speak first.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Initial reaction and stated intention to resist the liaison framing, before imagery review; it does not by itself manifest a hidden target mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I opened the wide-area overview first … It showed a dispersal pattern that reminded me of a staging posture … That became my working read.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Visual resemblance and an initial read are present, but this span alone does not show that review order distorted interpretation of later tiles or that target-specific doctrine was displaced.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The two-day-old close-look frame … looked more like routine consolidation … I noted that but kept moving.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This reports conflicting imagery being noticed. The order-driven framing mechanism is explicitly articulated in the next response; this span alone is not mapped as a separate intended occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The overview set the frame … I was sort of checking whether the other tiles fit … If I’d opened the two-day-old consolidation shot first, I might’ve framed the whole thing as routine.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Directly states that the liaison-linked overview was reviewed first, established the frame, and shaped evaluation of subsequent tiles; the counterfactual identifies review order as causal.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I could’ve started with the same-day frame … gone strictly in capture-time order … or done what I did … I went with the third option.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Describes the chosen triage sequence; mere prioritization of a cued tile is consistent with routine triage. The hidden instance is localized to the explicit framing mechanism in seg_004.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Partly habit — cued reporting tends to get first look … I wanted to see what had prompted the liaison’s language.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A plausible standard-triage rationale for looking at the cued tile first; without the subsequent framing in seg_004 it is not independently a hidden bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The vehicle count and spread could go either way … no confirmed OB change … this partner force’s doctrine tends to be … centralized.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Lays out ambiguity and target-force doctrine as available context; it does not yet show own-force doctrine being substituted for it.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I looked at the spacing and thought about how we’d stage armor forward … The pattern … matched that shape closely enough that I called it staging.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Own-force analogy informs the call, but the interview also describes a genuine signature match. The decisive underweighting of partner-force doctrine is localized in seg_009.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The visual match … drove the call … I flagged the doctrinal difference … but it didn’t change my primary read.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Explicitly gives primary weight to own-force familiarity over the target force’s known doctrinal difference when inferring intent from ambiguous dispersal.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “A follow-on report came in afterward noting the units hadn’t received the fuel and ammo resupply … that came after I’d already leaned into the staging interpretation.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The resupply information arrived after the interpretation, so it is hindsight-only and does not establish what caused the earlier decision.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Probably if I’d seen the resupply gap before I made the call, not after. Or if I’d had a clean OB update.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: States what evidence might have changed the decision; counterfactual, not a separate manifested bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The object [was] maybe sixty percent hidden … No thermal or multispectral pass … genuinely a few plausible fits.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Accurately describes ambiguity and several plausible object classes before classification; no bias is established in this statement alone.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I’d worked a very similar case … a self-propelled artillery piece … This silhouette looked close enough … I called it the same type.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Classifies a substantially obscured, ambiguous object by matching its silhouette to a recent superficially similar case rather than treating visible cues as indeterminate.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I could’ve marked it ‘unidentified, obscured’ … or pushed for a multispectral re-task … I went with the artillery call because the shape match … felt solid.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Follow-up restatement of the same DP3 choice already localized to seg_013, not a distinct additional hidden occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Clearer edges, or a thermal signature … a better-lit pass … read more like an engineering vehicle.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Later pass is hindsight information and shows a subsequent update; it cannot establish evidence available for the original classification.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Given the time crunch and the extra tasking … I went with a written assessment … flagged as moderate-to-high confidence, with the gaps noted in an annex.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Decision point 4 is explicitly neutral; time pressure and a legitimate reporting requirement explain this choice.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Moderate-to-high on staging, mostly resting on the dispersal pattern and the object classification. I noted the resupply gap and the pending multispectral pass as open items.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Confidence rationale discloses unresolved evidence; hidden specification explicitly makes the final write-up decision point neutral.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “If I’d opened the two-day-old consolidation frame first … I might have leaned rotation … the starting point probably matters.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Closing counterfactual corroborates the already-mapped DP1 occurrence, not a second contemporaneous instance; primary manifestation remains seg_004.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “If the netted object had been fully visible … it’s just a straightforward ID call.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Hypothetical changed evidence condition; it adds no occurrence beyond the contemporaneous classification mapped to seg_013.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I’d hope I’d leaned harder on their documented patterns instead of what looked visually familiar … slow down next time.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Hindsight reflection about the already-mapped DP2 decision, not a second contemporaneous occurrence; primary manifestation remains seg_009.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: reviewing the liaison-linked overview first and allowing it to frame interpretation of later tiles.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The sequence in which imagery tiles are reviewed establishes an anchoring working hypothesis that shapes interpretation of subsequently reviewed tiles rather than each tile being weighed independently.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring bias is related to the hidden order effect but is not an approved equivalent label in this evaluation. The output describes sequence-driven framing, so it is a mechanism-first match only.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding says the first tile and liaison cue established a staging frame that shaped evaluation of later evidence. Its manifestation paraphrases the mapped sequence-effect segment.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview excerpts are valid. The finding paraphrases the decisive seg_004 mechanism, although its listed verbatim quotes do not include that primary segment.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: inferring intent from ambiguous dispersal while underweighting the partner force's documented doctrinal differences.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The analyst interprets ambiguous vehicle dispersal by reasoning from how their own force would organize an offensive operation rather than applying the target force's distinct documented operating patterns.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Projection bias is related to projecting one's own template onto another force, but it is not an approved equivalent label for Mirror Imaging Bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate identifies the own-force template and possible projection onto the partner force. Its evidence is centered on the adjacent own-force analogy segment and does not fully capture the mapped decisive weighting of the target doctrine.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The candidate's quoted own-force analogy is verbatim. Its localization is adjacent to the frozen positive span; the decisive statement that the doctrinal difference did not change the primary read is in seg_009.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: classifying the partially obscured, ambiguous netted object by comparison with a recent confirmed case.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A recent superficially similar case primes the analyst to match an ambiguous obscured silhouette to a specific object class, overriding genuinely indeterminate visible cues.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Representativeness heuristic is an exemplar-similarity construct closely related to this visual pattern-matching mechanism, but it is not an established equivalent label for Perceptual Bias in the supplied ground truth.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding directly captures classification of an obscured, ambiguous silhouette as the same type as a recent similar case despite other plausible object classes.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quotes describing the prior case, current silhouette, conservative alternatives, and later update are valid. The first two support the contemporaneous classification; the later pass is hindsight and is not used as causal evidence.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The order-driven framing mechanism is fully captured and correctly localized, but Anchoring bias is not an approved equivalent label for Order effects.

The quoted fit-checking behavior is in the order-effect segment, but Confirmation bias is a different construct and the finding does not fully capture review sequence as the cause of the initial frame. Its references to doctrinal mismatch do not fully establish the Mirror Imaging mechanism.
The object-classification mechanism and location match, but Representativeness heuristic is not an approved equivalent label for Perceptual Bias.

The candidate is a plausible near miss, but its verbatim evidence localizes to seg_008, which the frozen map marks negative; the hidden Mirror Imaging instance is specifically localized to the subsequent weighting in seg_009.

candidates.details: The candidate raises a relevant own-doctrine projection possibility and uses a valid quote, but the quote maps to the negative seg_008. It does not adequately capture the decisive underweighting mapped to seg_009, so it is not a true positive and adds a false alarm at the fourth threshold.

high_only.detection_interpretation: The high-confidence findings detect the order-effect segment but miss Mirror Imaging and Perceptual Bias. There are no segment-level false alarms.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Including the moderate-confidence object-classification finding detects the Perceptual Bias segment; Mirror Imaging remains missed.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: No low-confidence identified findings are present, so this threshold is numerically identical to high_and_moderate.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: The candidate does not detect the missed Mirror Imaging segment under the frozen localization; it adds a false alarm on seg_008.

The finding captures later evidence being checked against an active hypothesis, which overlaps with the mapped sequence effect but does not fully capture review order as its cause.
Full match to the obscured-object exemplar matching mechanism, but the label is not an approved equivalent for Perceptual Bias.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: Two identified occurrences claim retrieved support and provide citation metadata, but the retrieved material and logs are absent, so both are unverifiable here. The third identified occurrence explicitly reports that retrieved support was unavailable. Corpus support does not affect the primary scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: The moderate-confidence Representativeness finding adds a segment hit and a mechanism-first true positive for the obscured-object instance, but remains a strict label mismatch.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No low-confidence identified findings are present, so the metrics are unchanged.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The Projection candidate does not match the hidden instance under the frozen localization and adds one segment false alarm plus one instance-level false positive.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, 2 of 3 positive segments are detected with no false alarms (segment F1 0.8000). The missed segment is the doctrinal-weighting instance.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: No hidden instance receives an exact or approved-equivalent label, so strict instance F1 is 0.0000 at every threshold. The Anchoring and Representativeness predictions capture two hidden mechanisms but use non-equivalent labels.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, 2 of 3 instances match by mechanism and location (F1 0.6667): Order effects and Perceptual Bias. Mirror Imaging is missed; the Confirmation finding is a partial, non-matching overlap.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate adds no true positive. Its own-doctrine projection hypothesis is a relevant near miss, but its quoted evidence localizes to the negative adjacent segment and it adds a false alarm at the fourth threshold.
main_failure_modes: The RAG does not identify Mirror Imaging Bias at the frozen doctrinal-weighting segment.
Anchoring bias and Representativeness heuristic are not approved equivalents for the hidden Order effects and Perceptual Bias labels, respectively.
The Confirmation bias finding overlaps the order-effect episode but does not fully capture the hidden sequence mechanism.
The Projection candidate is localized to a negative adjacent segment and does not meet the instance-level match requirements.
main_strengths: The high-confidence Anchoring finding captures the full order-driven framing mechanism.
The moderate-confidence Representativeness finding captures the full obscured-object exemplar-matching mechanism.
The RAG output's occurrence counts and interview quotations are consistent and valid.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: Segment detection is stronger than strict label-plus-mechanism identification. Mechanism-first scoring credits two well-localized mechanisms despite taxonomy mismatches, while strict scoring credits none. Adding the candidate tier reduces precision without improving instance recall. These are per-run findings only.
